title: t1: a two-token lookup table f(first, last) in a 2-layer, 2-head transformer
label: verified (function and a sufficient+necessary circuit); layer-0 head choice not unique
behavior: Input BOS + 4 tokens from 6 symbols (ids 2..7 = lo, po, nu, pe, ko, fo); the model outputs one symbol at the last position. All numbers are from the local-full backend (full precision).
summary: The model computes an unstructured 6x6 lookup table of the FIRST input token (pos 1) and the LAST input token (pos 4); the two middle tokens are ignored. The table reproduces the model's output on 600/600 held-out inputs across three unused seeds. Mechanism: layer-0 heads self-attend at pos 1 and enrich the x1 representation; layer-1 heads 1.0 and 1.1 both attend from pos 4 to pos 1 and move x1 to the last position; mlp0 and mlp1 hold the table and write most of the answer logits. Verified circuit: {0.0, 1.0, 1.1, mlp0, mlp1}. Head 0.1 is the weakest component and can be removed with no loss of accuracy, but it is not inert: it is a weaker duplicate of 0.0, and the pair is mutually redundant (either one suffices; removing both drops accuracy to 76%). No component of this model was found to be strictly without effect.
pseudocode:
def predict(tokens, prompt):
    # only pos 1 and pos 4 matter (E0005); table read off the model's outputs (E0001), 200/200 on V0001, V0002, V0003
    T = {2: [3, 6, 4, 3, 6, 3],
         3: [2, 7, 3, 3, 5, 4],
         4: [2, 6, 5, 7, 2, 5],
         5: [7, 7, 2, 7, 3, 6],
         6: [4, 3, 4, 6, 6, 6],
         7: [6, 3, 4, 4, 6, 5]}
    a = tokens[1]   # enriched at pos 1 by 0.0 (/0.1) (E0015, E0016), moved to pos 4 by 1.0 and 1.1 (E0012, E0009)
    d = tokens[4]   # already at the output position
    return T[a][d - 2]   # computed by mlp0 + mlp1 (E0010)

As strings (rows = first token, columns = last token lo po nu pe ko fo):
 lo: po ko nu po ko po
 po: lo fo po po pe nu
 nu: lo ko pe fo lo pe
 pe: fo fo lo fo po ko
 ko: nu po nu ko ko ko
 fo: ko po nu nu ko pe

claims.text: The model performs the behaviour perfectly on its own labels: accuracy 1.0, mean logit difference 15.1.

The output is a function of the first and last input tokens only. Patching the residual stream at pos 2 or pos 3 changes the metric by less than 0.4%, while pos 1 and pos 4 carry 0.54 and 0.44 at layer 0.
The function is the 6x6 lookup table given in the pseudocode: it matches the model on 200/200 held-out inputs in each of three unused seeds (null agreement about 0.18).

x1 is still at pos 1 when layer 1 starts (resid_pre.1 @ pos 1 effect 0.50) and is moved to the last position by heads 1.0 and 1.1, which attend pos 4 -> pos 1 with weight 0.75 and 0.72; denoising them restores 36% and 28% of the metric.
The two movers are the main route but joint mean-ablation leaves 37% of the logit difference, more than the predicted 30% (prediction refuted); single ablations leave 62-69%.

The MLPs carry the table: denoising mlp0 output restores 79% and mlp1 74% of the metric; mean-ablating either leaves 22% / 30%. Heads write only about 2.9 of 15.1 logits directly and the direct-path effect of 1.0/1.1 is 0.11/0.07 of their 0.36/0.28 total, so the heads act mostly through mlp1.

Layer-0 heads are not inert (two predictions refuted): denoising 0.0 / 0.1 restores 19% / 11%, most of it (13% / 9%) through the value input of the mover heads; at pos 1 they self-attend with weight 0.64 / 0.61, i.e. they enrich the x1 representation that is later copied.

Core circuit {1.0, 1.1, mlp0, mlp1} is necessary (ablated: accuracy 0.225, fraction -0.01) but not sufficient alone: with both layer-0 heads mean-ablated the fraction is 0.65 (bar 0.70) and accuracy 0.76. This verification failed.

Circuit {0.0, 1.0, 1.1, mlp0, mlp1} passes all checks on held-out seed 102: circuit ablated -> accuracy 0.22, fraction 0.02; everything else (head 0.1) ablated -> accuracy 1.00, fraction 0.89; all effects beyond the null controls.

The layer-0 head is not uniquely identified: the control circuit with 0.1 instead of 0.0 also passes (only 0.0 ablated -> accuracy 1.00, fraction 0.82). The two layer-0 heads are a redundant pair with 0.0 the stronger (single mean-ablation 0.82 vs 0.88).

nodes.label: mlp0: token features for the table
mlp1: table lookup f(x1,x4) at pos 4

limitations: No component is strictly inert in my measurements. Head 0.1 is the best candidate for 'not part of the circuit' (removing it keeps accuracy 1.0 and 89% of the margin), but swapping the roles of 0.0 and 0.1 also verifies (V0003), so which layer-0 head belongs in the circuit is a matter of degree, not a clean cut.
Three of ten scored predictions were refuted (E0007, E0009, E0015) and one was inconclusive because mlp_out patching is not per-position on this backend (E0010).
MLP-mediated edges (mlp0 -> movers, mlp0 -> mlp1) are inferred from layer-level patching and ablation; path patching with MLP senders errored, so those edges are not directly tested.
The split of work between mlp0 and mlp1 inside the table lookup is not resolved; I did not look for neurons or features.
Residual 37% of margin after ablating both movers is unexplained: it may be what x4 alone supports, or x1 leaking through the diffuse layer-0 attention at pos 4.
The table has no formula I could find; it is reported as a lookup. All 36 cells were observed in the seed-0 data.
open_questions: Is the table a composition of simpler maps (e.g. a function of features of x1 and x4) that mlp0 and mlp1 factor between them?
Why does the model keep two movers and two enrichers: pure redundancy from training, or do they specialise by token?
What exactly does mlp0 contribute at pos 1 versus pos 4?
overall_status: partial / not verified · verified (function and a sufficient+necessary circuit); layer-0 head choice not unique

refuted_predictions.hypothesis: Heads 1.0 and 1.1 are jointly the (redundant) route by which x1 reaches the last position; removing both destroys the behaviour.

prediction.statement: jointly mean-ablating 1.0 and 1.1 leaves at most 30% of the clean logit difference

refuted_predictions.hypothesis: Layer-0 heads do not carry input-specific information that the output depends on: denoising head 0.0 alone recovers almost nothing, whereas layer-1 heads recover a sizeable share.

prediction.statement: patching head 0.0's clean output into the corrupt run restores less than 10% of the metric

refuted_predictions.hypothesis: Layer-0 heads influence the answer mainly through mlp0 (same layer), not by writing directly into the value input of the layer-1 mover heads: the direct path 0.0 -> {1.0,1.1}.v carries less than a third of 0.0's total 0.186 denoising effect.

prediction.statement: direct path 0.0 -> value input of 1.0/1.1 restores less than 6% of the metric
